description: Approximately 50 children are backed over by vehicles every week. Why backovers happen and the legal challenges families face when a relative is at fault.
shortAnswer: Drivers backing over children (Backovers) is the most common form of non-traffic fatalities for children under the age of 15. These children are injured and die because adults (70% of the time parents or relatives) do not see them when backing up.

faq.q: Why do backover accidents involving young children happen?
faq.a: Backover and Frontover injuries occur because all vehicles have blind zones – the area behind (or in front of) a vehicle that the person sitting in the driver's seat can not see. Most of these incidents occur in the child's own driveway or in a parking lot. The typical age of victims is between 12-23 months (young toddlers).

faq.q: Can you sue a family member in Georgia for backing over a child?
faq.a: The long standing rule in Georgia is that there is intra-family tort immunity (which means that generally speaking you can not sue a close family member for negligence). Yet in recent decades Georgia Courts have held that intra-family tort immunity is no longer a blanket defense in injury cases.

faq.q: Will car insurance pay when the child hurt in a backover is the policyholder's family member?
faq.a: The relevant policy of insurance may contain an exclusion to the liability coverage when the injured or killed party was a family member of the policyholder. Such provisions (known as "family exclusion clauses") may be void as against the public policy of the State of Georgia.
